Frequently Asked Questions - Pakistan Tax

How much tax is deducted from salary in Pakistan?

Tax deduction from salary in Pakistan depends on your taxable income and FBR tax slabs. For salaried individuals, the monthly tax is calculated based on annual taxable income after deductions. Use our Pakistan income tax calculator to estimate your exact monthly tax deduction.

What is the tax-free limit for salary in Pakistan?

The tax-free limit for salaried individuals in Pakistan is PKR 600,000 per year for the 2024/25 tax year. This means if your annual salary is below PKR 600,000, you may not owe any income tax. Use our Pakistan tax calculator to check your tax-free threshold.

What are the FBR tax slabs for FY 2026–27?

FBR tax slabs for salaried individuals in Pakistan range from 0% to 35% based on annual taxable income. The slabs are progressive, with higher incomes taxed at higher rates. For the latest FY 2026–27 slabs, use our Pakistan income tax calculator which is updated with the latest FBR rates.

How is monthly salary tax calculated in Pakistan?

Monthly salary tax in Pakistan is calculated by dividing your annual taxable income by 12, then applying the applicable FBR tax slab. The employer deducts tax at source under Section 159. Use our Pakistan salary tax calculator to compute your exact monthly tax.

Are medical and house rent allowances taxable?

Medical allowance and house rent allowance (HRA) in Pakistan are generally taxable as part of your salary income. However, certain exemptions and deductions may apply. Use our Pakistan income tax calculator to understand how these allowances affect your tax.

How do I calculate tax if I change jobs mid-year?

If you change jobs mid-year, your total income from both employers is combined for the year, and tax is calculated on the aggregate income. Each employer may deduct tax separately, which could result in over-deduction. Use our Pakistan tax calculator to compute your annual tax liability and claim a refund if needed.

Who qualifies as a "Salaried Individual" for FBR?

A salaried individual for FBR purposes is any person receiving income from employment, pension, or annuity. This includes government employees, private sector employees, and expatriates working in Pakistan. The Pakistan tax calculator applies to all salaried individuals regardless of employment sector.

What is the tax rate for freelancers and sole proprietors in Pakistan?

Freelancers and sole proprietors in Pakistan are taxed at the same progressive rates as individuals, ranging from 0% to 35% on net business income. They must file annual income tax returns and may be required to pay advance tax. Use our business income tax calculator Pakistan to estimate your tax.

Can I use an online tax calculator for official tax filing?

Our online tax calculator Pakistan is designed for estimation and planning purposes only. For official tax filing, you must file through the FBR Iris portal or consult a qualified tax professional. Our calculators provide accurate estimates but do not constitute official tax advice.

What is the penalty for non-filing tax in Pakistan?

The penalty for non-filing of tax returns in Pakistan can be substantial. FBR may impose penalties up to PKR 100,000 or more, and non-filers face higher withholding tax rates on banking, property, and vehicle transactions. Use our Pakistan tax calculator to estimate your liability and avoid penalties.
